title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — entered by propagation; leprosy analogy; Non entis
pass_a_gloss: Who but a Pelagian fails to see sin entered humans by natural propagation as we are begotten—and so was not fetched from outside into those already born? It is said to have entered us because it truly is inside us, yet not from creation or human nature itself, but from elsewhere: the serpent's temptation and the first man's actual. So through one man that vice entered human nature where it was not and ought not to be, and with nature into us all—which cannot be said of the actual. What is innate, if not from nature, may still be said to have entered children through parents: as leprosy or gout through a parent, though the child has leprosy from birth. Not earlier in time, yet earlier by nature we were than we were corrupt—corruption of nature cannot but be later than nature. If we were not before we were corrupt, and corruption follows: of a non-being there are no accidents.
pass_b_english: Who also, unless he is a Pelagian, does not understand that sin entered into humans by natural propagation as soon as we are begotten, and therefore was not brought from outside into those already born? namely it is said to have entered into us, because it truly is inside us, and yet is not from creation, or from human nature itself, but from elsewhere, from the serpent's temptation and the first man's actual sin. And so truly through one man that vice entered into human nature where before it was not, nor ought to be, and together with nature into us all, which cannot be said of actual sin. What therefore is innate, if it is not from nature, nothing can prohibit that it be said to have entered through parents into children. So it can be said that through a parent leprosy or gout entered into children, although leprosy is in the children from birth. Not indeed earlier in time, but earlier yet by nature we were than we were corrupt. For corruption of nature cannot but be later than nature itself. But if we were not earlier than we were corrupt, and corruption follows, Of a non-being there are no accidents.
source_text: Quis etiam, nisi sit Pelagianus, non intelligit peccatum intrasse in homines propagatione naturali simul ac gignimur, ac proinde in genitos non fuisse foris delatum? nempe dicitur in nos intrasse, quia revera intra nos est, nec tamen est a creatione, aut ab ipsa humana natura, sed aliunde, a tentatione serpentis & peccato primi hominis actuali. Itaque revera per unum hominem vitium illud in naturam humanam ubi antea non erat, nec esse debebat, intravit, & una cum natura in nos omnes, id quod de peccato actuali dici non potest. Quod igitur innatum est, id si non est a natura, quominus per parentes in liberos introiisse dicatur, nihil potest prohibere. Sic potest dici per parentem in liberos lepra aut podagra intraisse, quamvis lepra insit liberis ab ortu. Non quidem prius tempore, at prius tamen natura fuimus quam corrupti fuimus. Non potest enim corruptio naturae non esse posterior ipsa natura. Caeterum si prius non fuimus quam corrupti fuimus, & corruptio sequitur, Non entis nulla sunt accidentia.
